mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let's take a moment to really let this sink in. Operating Instructions isn’t just a story about a baby’s first year—it’s a tribute to the wild, beautiful, and oh-so-human journey of parenthood. Through the eyes of a single mom, you get to feel the raw beginnings, the ache that comes with loss, the strength that comes from community, and those quiet, everyday acts of courage that build a family from the ground up. The road isn’t straight or simple. It’s tangled with doubt, lit up by unexpected joy, and shaped by the slow, steady work of learning to trust yourself. So, if you’re in the thick of new parenthood—or facing any big life change—here’s what you can carry with you: Community grows from those small, brave moments when you let yourself be seen, and when you show up for someone else. Resilience? It’s not about never feeling scared. It’s about showing up anyway, even when you’re not sure you can. And self-discovery isn’t a finish line. It’s the ongoing permission to shift, to change, and to keep growing. Asking for help doesn’t mean you’re weak—it means you’re wise enough to know we’re better together. And in the end, it’s those ordinary moments—the laughter, the messes, the small acts of care—that matter most. There’s no perfect way to parent, to grieve, or to become who you’re meant to be. The path will twist, you’ll stumble, and that’s okay. You are not alone. Each day is a fresh start—another chance to show up, to love, and to keep going. Trust that the little things you do—holding a hand, sharing a meal, forgiving yourself—are more than enough. You don’t need all the answers. What matters is being present for the questions, and letting love guide you forward. So whatever your journey looks like, remember: you are capable, you are resilient, and you are enough.
